## Block Thomas sweep and back substitution: one serial pass up, one down, per column (`ForwardSweep`) {#sec-ch07-vic-sweep}

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What it does.** Solves the block-tridiagonal system of @eq-ch07-vic-blocks for one column: a forward
elimination from the first layer to the last, then a back substitution.

**Switch.** As for the assembly; $N=3$ or $N=5$.

**Order.** A direct solve, exact up to round-off.

**Defining equation.** @eq-ch07-vic-sweep.
:::

The right-hand side is the explicit increment of the stage over the step. So the sweep returns the corrected
increment $\delta = (I+\Delta t\,J)^{-1}\Delta\mathbf U$, which is the explicit one when $\Delta t\to0$. Every
block it inverts is first factored by `ludcmp` with the pivot guard of @sec-ch07-vic-pivot. A refused block
marks the whole column as failed.

### Derivation

With $r_i = \Delta\mathbf U_i/\Delta t$ in the solved variables, block Gaussian elimination without pivoting
between blocks gives, for $i = 0, 1, \ldots, n-1$, with $a_{-1}'$ and $\delta_{-1}$ taken as zero,

$$
\begin{aligned}
a_i' &= \big(a_i - b_i a_{i-1}'\big)^{-1} c_i , \\
\delta_i &= \big(a_i - b_i a_{i-1}'\big)^{-1}\big(r_i - b_i\,\delta_{i-1}\big) ,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch07-vic-sweep}

and then $\delta_i \leftarrow \delta_i - a_i'\,\delta_{i+1}$ from $i=n-2$ down to 0. On 60 layers the two passes
match a dense solve to $4\times10^{-16}$ relative for $N=3$ and $N=5$ [check
`src/snapy_report/ch07/vic_sweep_check.py`, output `vic_sweep_check.out`, `[C1]`]. With the assembled blocks the
result is $(I+\Delta t\,J)^{-1}\Delta\mathbf U$, and it tends to $\Delta\mathbf U$ as $\Delta t\to0$ (`[C2]`).

The first entry of $r_i$ is the total density increment, dry plus all species, over $\Delta t$. The species are
not in the system; they follow in @sec-ch07-vic-redistribute.

In the code, @eq-ch07-vic-sweep is `ForwardSweep` ({{< code src/implicit/forward_sweep_impl.h ForwardSweep >}}) followed by `vic_backward_substitute` ({{< code src/implicit/vic_redistribute_impl.h vic_backward_substitute >}}).

### Numerical method

See @fig-ch07-vic-sweep for the two passes.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch07-vic-sweep
#| fig-cap: "The block-tridiagonal matrix of one column (green: the diagonal blocks $a_i$; sky blue: $b_i$, $c_i$) and the two passes that solve it. The forward sweep (orange) runs from the first row to the last and factors each eliminated block with ludcmp, refusing it when a pivot ratio is at most $8N\\epsilon$; the back substitution (blue) runs from the last row to the first."
#| fig-alt: "A six-by-six block-tridiagonal matrix on the left, and on the right a downward orange arrow with the forward formulas and an upward blue arrow with the back-substitution formula."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch07.fig_vic_sweep import make_fig
make_fig()
```

`ForwardSweep` builds the right-hand side `rhs` of each layer from the explicit increment, with the density row
summed over the species ({{< code src/implicit/forward_sweep_impl.h ForwardSweep >}}). For $N=5$ it factors the eliminated block and
solves for $a_i'$ and $\delta_i$ together with the multi-column `lubksb`
({{< code src/implicit/forward_sweep_impl.h ForwardSweep >}}). For $N=3$ it checks the factorisation with `ludcmp` and
keeps the explicit inverse ({{< code src/implicit/forward_sweep_impl.h ForwardSweep >}}). After every layer it checks that $a_i'$ and $\delta_i$ are
finite. On any failure, `vic_fail_column` fills every $\delta$ of the column with NaN and the sweep returns
({{< code src/implicit/vic_solve_failure.h vic_fail_column >}}). `vic_backward_substitute` skips a column whose first $\delta$ is not
finite ({{< code src/implicit/vic_redistribute_impl.h vic_backward_substitute >}}). So a failed column is never partly back-substituted
(`[C3]`).

The dispatch `vic_solve_cpu` runs both passes per column ({{< code src/implicit/implicit_dispatch.cpp vic_solve_cpu >}}). Each layer depends on
every right-hand side below and above it (`[C4]`), so the column is serial; the parallelism is across columns.
On CUDA the sweep is one thread per column, and the assembly and the final cell update are one thread per cell.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
There is no pivoting between blocks. The sweep relies on the $I/\Delta t$ diagonal and the upwind $|\hat A|$
to keep the eliminated blocks regular.
:::

1. **No accuracy test.** No ctest compares the sweep with a dense solve; the ctests check refusal and
   finiteness only.
2. **One rank per column.** The commented-out send and receive in the sweep are the trace of a distributed column
   that is not supported (@sec-ch07-vic-options).
